privacy_intro: VAZHI is built so that the awkward questions never arise. Wherever we could avoid holding something about you, we did — and where we could not, we made sure it never leaves your device.
privacy_demo_note: This is a demonstration build. There is no server, no database, and no account: everything below describes how the application behaves in your browser right now.
privacy_hold_memory: Passenger names, ages, and genders live in memory for the length of one booking and are cleared when you close the tab.
privacy_hold_device: Your bookings, comfort preferences, theme, and language stay on this device so your trips survive a reload.
privacy_hold_route: Route criteria — where you are travelling from and to, the date, and how many seats — are the only things that appear in a web address.
privacy_never_url: Never puts a passenger's name, age, gender, or contact detail in a URL.
privacy_never_storage: Never writes passenger details to storage, cookies, or a saved file.
privacy_never_log: Never logs passenger details to the console or to an analytics service — there is no analytics in this build.
privacy_never_id: Never asks for a government ID, and never asks for medical information.
privacy_never_share: Never shows one traveller anything about another. Comfort signals describe areas of a bus, not the people in them.
privacy_crew_body: A conductor sees a seat, a booking reference, and whether that booking has boarded. Their screens have no field for a name, an age, a gender, or a phone number, so those details cannot reach a crew device even by mistake.
privacy_comfort_body: Seat suggestions describe an area of the coach — near the entrance, a quieter section, a step-free seat. Where VAZHI notes that women passengers are seated nearby, it is describing a part of the bus, never a person, and it is a preference indicator rather than a guarantee. Seating may change before departure.
privacy_control_body: Clearing your browser's site data removes everything VAZHI has kept on this device. Nothing is held anywhere else, because there is nowhere else.
a11y_intro: A bus stand is a hard place to use a phone: bright sun, one free hand, a bag on the other shoulder, and a coach about to leave. VAZHI is built for that, not for a quiet desk.
a11y_atm_body: One switch on the search form raises the whole journey. It floats step-free boarding points to the top of the results, ranks step-free seats first on the coach plan, and keeps that choice for the rest of the booking. It never asks why you have turned it on and never records a reason.
a11y_built_keyboard: Every control is reachable and operable from a keyboard, including the location picker, the seat plan, and the conductor's boarding screen.
a11y_built_focus: A visible focus ring follows you, thick enough to find on a sunlit screen.
a11y_built_targets: Every button, seat, and list row is at least 44 by 44 pixels.
a11y_built_contrast: Colours meet WCAG AA contrast in both light and dark themes, and colour is never the only way a state is shown — seats also carry a shape, a glyph, or a position.
a11y_built_labels: Form fields carry real labels, errors are announced, and focus moves to the first field that needs fixing.
a11y_built_motion: Motion is reduced automatically when your system asks for it, and can be turned down manually in travel preferences.
a11y_built_text: A larger-text option scales the whole interface rather than one page.
a11y_built_language: Every screen is available in English and Tamil, including error messages and status announcements.
a11y_limits_title: Where we are not there yet
a11y_limits_body: This is a demonstration build. The maps convey route shape visually and are described in text beside them, but they are not yet fully explorable with a screen reader. Intermediate stop names on the live-tracking view are shown in English only.
a11y_feedback_body: Accessibility problems are bugs. In a live service this page would carry a direct route to report one; in this demonstration build there is no inbox behind it.

payani_a_greeting: Vanakkam! Ask me anything about booking a bus, your ticket, seats, or travelling with VAZHI.
payani_a_book:
To book a bus on VAZHI:

1. Choose your starting point and destination.
2. Pick your travel date.
3. Search and choose a service from the results.
4. Select your seat or berth.
5. Enter passenger details.
6. Review and pay.

Your ticket and booking reference are issued as soon as payment succeeds.
payani_a_search:
Open Explore, choose where you are travelling from and to, pick a date, and search. You will see the services running that day with their times, fares and seats left.

You can filter by departure time, price, air conditioning and coach type.
payani_a_seat:
After choosing a service, the seat map opens.

1. Grey seats are taken; the rest are free.
2. Tap a seat to select it, tap again to release it.
3. Window and aisle seats are marked, so you can pick what you prefer.

Your seats are held for a few minutes while you finish paying.
payani_a_sleeper:
A sleeper service has berths you can lie down on instead of seats. They come in two tiers — lower and upper — shown as separate sections on the seat map.

Lower berths are easier to climb into; upper berths are usually quieter.
payani_a_payment:
Payment happens in a secure Razorpay window, where you can pay by UPI, card, net banking or a wallet.

VAZHI never sees or stores your card, UPI or bank details — they go straight to the payment provider. Your booking is only confirmed once the payment is verified.
payani_a_pnr:
A PNR is your booking reference — the short code that identifies your ticket, like VZ-A1B2C3D4E5.

Show it to the conductor when boarding, and quote it if you ever need help with a booking. You will find it on your ticket and in My Trips.
payani_a_ticket:
Open My Trips to see all your bookings, then choose one to view the ticket.

A copy is also emailed to the address on your account when you book. If it has not arrived, check your spam folder.
payani_a_qr:
Every ticket carries a QR code. The conductor scans it when you board to check your booking — it is the quickest way through the door.

If the code will not scan, the booking reference printed underneath works just as well.
payani_a_boarding:
Boarding is getting on the bus at the start of your journey.

Go to the boarding point shown on your ticket, find the platform number, and show your QR code or booking reference to the conductor. Arrive a few minutes early — boarding closes shortly before departure.
payani_a_cancel:
To cancel a booking:

1. Open My Trips.
2. Select the booking you want to cancel.
3. Choose Cancel booking and confirm.

A cancellation fee is deducted and the rest is refunded. Once the bus has departed, a booking can no longer be cancelled.
payani_a_refund:
When you cancel, a cancellation fee is deducted and the remaining amount is refunded to the way you paid.

You can follow its progress on the refund screen, and every refund also appears in your transaction history.
payani_a_track:
Open My Trips and choose Track live on an upcoming journey to see its progress along the route.

Please note this is a simulated view for demonstration — it is not a live GPS feed from the vehicle.
payani_a_transactions: Your account has a Transaction history screen listing every payment and refund, with the amount, date and booking reference for each one.
payani_a_account:
You need a traveller account to book. Register with your email address and a password, then sign in.

Your email address is also where your tickets are sent, so use one you check.
payani_a_language: VAZHI is available in English and Tamil. Use the language control at the top of the screen to switch — everything, including this chat, changes with it.
payani_a_accessible:
Turn on Accessible Travel Mode in your travel preferences. Services with a step-free boarding point are marked, and suitable seats are highlighted when you choose one.

You can also note an assistance requirement in the passenger details step.
payani_a_concession:
You can note a concession category for each passenger in the passenger details step.

Carry proof of eligibility when you travel, as the conductor may ask to see it.
payani_a_luggage:
You can bring a reasonable amount of luggage. Larger bags travel in the luggage compartment and smaller ones with you.

Exact allowances vary by operator, so check with the conductor if you are carrying something unusually large.
payani_a_missed:
If you miss your bus, the ticket cannot be used for a later service and the booking cannot be cancelled after departure.

You would need to book again for the next available service. Arriving a few minutes before departure avoids this.
payani_a_vazhi:
VAZHI is a public bus booking service for Tamil Nadu.

You can search services between towns, choose a seat or berth, pay securely, and carry your ticket on your phone. Conductors scan it when you board.

I am Payani, and I can explain how any part of it works.
payani_a_help:
For anything I cannot answer, the Help section has guidance, and the Privacy page explains how your information is handled.

If a booking has gone wrong, keep your booking reference to hand — it identifies your ticket.
payani_a_cannot:
I can explain how it works, but I cannot do it for you — I answer questions only.

To book, use Explore to search and choose a service. To cancel, open My Trips, select the booking and choose Cancel booking.
payani_a_unknown:
I do not have enough information to answer that accurately. Please check the relevant VAZHI section.

I can help with booking, seats, tickets, PNRs, boarding, payment, cancellation and refunds.
